corrections: Replaced generic low-wing airframe with independently measured G36 stations, four true side-window apertures, wraparound windscreen, long six-seat fuselage, standard tail, three-blade stock propeller and retracting tricycle gear.

Used uniform side/front/top overlays. Expanded the pilot side window, raised all passenger-window lower edges, moved the wing aft 0.18 m and corrected rudder extent to match overall length. Wing planform now closely follows the manufacturer drawing with published six-degree dihedral; span, length, tail span and wheel track were checked separately.

Built the G1000/GFC700 panel from the manufacturer diagram, with twin 10.4-inch units, central audio strip, right-hand vertical standby stack, glareshield compass, switch/breaker subpanels, gear/flap controls and lamps, glovebox, dual Beechcraft yokes and quadrant pedestal. Brochure photographs supplied physical controls, panel depth and upholstery details.

Added six seats with the middle pair facing aft, headrests, belts, sidewall cupholders, folded table, overhead ventilation, cowl details, wingtip/landing lights, vortex generators, skin divisions and rivet rows.

Added reusable G1000 physical/display helpers while preserving independently authored panel placement. Wired live speed tape/digits, attitude, three-pointer standby altimeter, true heading, climb, 2700-RPM tachometer, throttle, yokes and pedals. Gear lamps distinguish down-locked, transit, up and missing data; legs rotate inward/aft with simulated travel.
reviewNotes.visual: Individually inspected four turntables, three-quarter ground, pilot, cabin and wide cabin plus current side/front/top/panel overlays. Inspected zero, 120-knot/3500-foot/2500-RPM cruise with gear up, 205-knot/12500-foot/2700-RPM upper-range with gear in transit, and negative-altitude/missing speed/RPM/gear states. Confirmed independent pitch/bank, blank missing readouts and gear lamps in rendered images.
limitations: Manufacturer views are schematic and disagree in fin height and horizontal-tail elevation. Model honors the printed 2.6162 m height; uniform side scale suggests approximately 2.8 m and front scale approximately 3.1 m. Horizontal-tail elevation follows the side drawing rather than the higher front-view depiction. No reference was stretched to conceal these residuals.

Wing root fillets, rounded tail tips, curved windscreen sections and exact cabin cross-sections remain polygonal approximations. Small door/window corner and gear-door contour residuals remain. Rivet lines follow visible skin divisions, not a manufacturing fastener map.

Panel diagram omits yokes and pedestal; their depth is estimated from brochure photographs. Fine switch legends, upholstery curvature and the pedestal connection remain simplified. Manufacturer cockpit imagery is local study only; no suitably licensed photograph of this exact G36 cockpit was verified for redistribution. The licensed exterior photo and all manufacturer pixels remain unshipped.

Live displays provide a useful subset rather than a complete Garmin simulation. Speed is TAS, altitude geometric world elevation (GEO FT), heading true and RPM normalized simulated propeller speed scaled to 2700. Pressure/IAS, magnetic errors, engine governor, oil/fuel/electrical systems, navigation, vacuum and warning logic beyond gear travel are not simulated; unavailable readings stay blank or INOP. Standby-speed calibration is approximate.

Propeller/mixture levers, trim and most switches are not interactive. Gear travel has simplified linked doors and no detailed wheel-well mechanism; three green lamps share the single simulated gear-position sensor. Flap approach lamp can indicate 40-percent travel but current pilot input selects only up/down.

controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.
